assignments.title: Reading Journal Setup (your Module 3 home base)
assignments.html:
📁 Set up your Reading Journal

This is your home base for the whole module: one Word document where you keep your reading notes, new words, and your growing ideas about the knights. You set up the file in the Week-1 lesson "Reading Journal in M365"; this assignment is where you build its four sections and turn it in the first time. It takes about ten minutes. You will read King Arthur and His Knights of the Round Table from your own copy of the book as you fill it in.

📁 M365 SKILL STEP

  • ☐ Open the Word doc you created in the "Reading Journal in M365" lesson (or make it now: open Word

from your school account)

  • ☐ Confirm it is named LastName_FirstName_ReadingJournal_M3_ELA6
  • ☐ Saved to OneDrive → Optima → ELA → ELA6
  • ☐ Build the four sections below using Heading 1 for each section title
  • ☐ Submit it here via the Microsoft OneDrive tab

M365 Skill You're Practicing: Applying Heading styles to organize a Word document (Word — MOS Core)

Build these four sections (Heading 1 each):

  1. The Big Question — copy this in and leave room to answer it as the module goes:

"What makes a good knight?" Write your first answer in 2–3 sentences today; you will revise it at the end.

  1. My Word Bank — a running list. Each week, add the new words you met in the reading and a short

definition in your own words. (You will pull from here when you write.)

  1. Week-by-Week Notes — a Heading 2 for each week (Week 1 … Week 6). Under each week, keep the details

you noticed, your close-reading observations, and anything you might use in your writing. This is where your weekly journal entries go.

  1. My Building Claim — one place where your interpretation grows. This is the seed of your comparison

essay. Start a sentence like "So far, I think the better knight is ______ because…" and revise it as you meet more knights and the story changes your mind.

✅ Done when

  • ☐ The file is named correctly and saved to your ELA6 OneDrive folder.
  • ☐ All four sections exist, each under a Heading 1.
  • ☐ You have written a first answer to the Big Question and submitted via the OneDrive tab.

quizzes.description:
Week 1 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · Module 3 · Week 1
20 points10 questionsOpen notesOne try
Questions 1 to 5 · Grammar
Nouns and pronouns
 
Questions 6 to 10 · Words
sovereigndestinyvaloranvilchivalry
Done when
 
☐All 10 answered
☐Submitted (one try)
☐I read the feedback on any I missed

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is a noun? "The young squire drew the shining sword."
questions.feedback_correct: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea: squire names a person.
questions.feedback_incorrect: "Young" and "shining" describe; "drew" is an action. Which word names someone?

questions.text: A pronoun is a word that

answers.text: takes the place of a noun

questions.feedback_correct: Right: a pronoun (he, she, it, they) stands in for a noun so you need not repeat it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Describing is an adjective's job and action is a verb's. A pronoun replaces a noun.

questions.text: In "Arthur drew the sword, and it shone in the light," the pronoun it points back to
questions.feedback_correct: Right: it stands for sword, the thing that shone. The noun a pronoun points to is its antecedent.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A pronoun must point to a noun already named. What is the bright thing Arthur drew?

questions.text: Which pronoun correctly matches the noun? "The knights kept their oaths, and ______ defended Logres."
questions.feedback_correct: Right: knights is plural, so the matching pronoun is they.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A pronoun must match its noun in number. How many knights are there?

questions.text: Which sentence has the clearest pronoun (no confusion about who is meant)?

answers.text: Arthur told Kay that he was king.
He told him that he was king.
Arthur told Kay that he had the sword.
Arthur told Kay that Arthur was king.

questions.feedback_correct: Right: with two men named, repeating Arthur removes all doubt about who is king.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When two people are named, "he" can point to either one. Which choice leaves no doubt?

questions.text: Once Arthur draws the sword, he is named the true sovereign of Britain. A sovereign is
questions.feedback_correct: Right: a sovereign is the supreme ruler; Arthur becomes Britain's king.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A sovereign is a person who rules, not a weapon or an object. Arthur is named the true ruler.

questions.text: Merlin hid the infant because he knew the child's destiny was to be king. Destiny means

answers.text: the future a person seems meant to fulfill

questions.feedback_correct: Right: a destiny is the future a person seems meant for; Arthur's was to be king.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Destiny is about the future a person is meant for, not an object or an event.

questions.text: The knights of Logres were praised for their valor in battle. Valor means
questions.feedback_correct: Right: valor is great courage, especially in danger or battle.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Valor is about bravery, not wealth, cooking, or laziness.

questions.text: The sword stood thrust into an anvil of iron. An anvil is

answers.text: a heavy iron block a blacksmith hammers metal against

questions.feedback_correct: Right: an anvil is the heavy iron block a smith works metal on; the sword was fixed in it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: An anvil is a blacksmith's heavy iron block, not a cloth, a crown, or a lake.

questions.text: Which sentence uses chivalry correctly?

answers.text: "He sharpened his chivalry before the battle."
"The chivalry rose from the lake holding a sword."
"She wore a chivalry of white samite."
"The knights lived by the code of chivalry: honor, courage, and courtesy."

questions.feedback_correct: Right: chivalry is the code of honor, courage, and courtesy knights lived by.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Chivalry is a code of conduct, not a weapon, a person, or a piece of clothing.

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is the verb? "The lady offered Gawain a green lace."
questions.feedback_correct: Offered shows the action.
questions.feedback_incorrect: One of these names a person, one names a thing, one describes. Which word shows the action?

questions.text: What tense is the verb in "Gawain will keep his oath at the Green Chapel"?
questions.feedback_correct: Will keep has not happened yet: future.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Has the keeping happened yet? Look at will.

questions.text: Which sentence keeps a steady tense?

answers.text: Gawain met the lord merrily and gave him three kisses.
Gawain met the lord merrily and gives him three kisses.
Gawain meets the lord merrily and gave him three kisses.
Gawain meet the lord merrily and gives him three kisses.

questions.feedback_correct: Met and gave are both past.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the choice where both verbs are past tense.

questions.text: Which change replaces a weak verb with a stronger, more exact one?

answers.text: "The Green Knight went out of the hall" → "The Green Knight moved out of the hall"
"The Green Knight went out of the hall" → "The Green Knight came out of the hall"
"The Green Knight went out of the hall" → "The Green Knight galloped out of the hall"
"The Green Knight went out of the hall" → "The Green Knight got out of the hall"

questions.feedback_correct: Galloped shows exactly how he left.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Three choices swap one vague verb for another. Which one paints the action?

questions.text: Which fixes the tense slip in "Gawain hid the lace and says nothing to the lord"?

answers.text: Gawain hides the lace and said nothing to the lord.
Gawain hid the lace and said nothing to the lord.
Gawain hid the lace and will say nothing to the lord.
Gawain hidden the lace and says nothing to the lord.

questions.feedback_correct: Hid and said: both past, steady.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sentence starts in the past with hid. Keep the second verb there too.

questions.text: Gawain says, "My lord king and noble uncle, grant me a boon!" A boon is
questions.feedback_correct: He asks Arthur for a favor: to let the adventure be his.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read what he asks for in the next sentence.

questions.text: Gawain tells the lord, "May God bless you for your hospitality." Hospitality is

answers.text: a friendly welcome and care given to a guest
a place where horses are kept
a feast held on New Year's Day

questions.feedback_correct: The lord welcomes him, feeds him and gives him a warm room.
questions.feedback_incorrect: What has the lord just given Gawain?

questions.text: "This proved too great a temptation for Gawain." A temptation is

answers.text: a strong pull to do something you know you should not

questions.feedback_correct: The lace pulls Gawain toward breaking his bargain.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The lace is the charm. What did the lace do to Gawain?

questions.text: Gawain says, "For cowardice and covetousness I betrayed my oath of knighthood." Covetousness means

answers.text: being too afraid to face danger
wanting to keep something for yourself too much

questions.feedback_correct: He wanted to keep the lace for himself.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Being too afraid is cowardice, the other word in his sentence.

questions.text: The Green Knight says, "You have borne your penance, and are quite absolved and forgiven." Penance is

answers.text: a written order from a king
something hard you accept to make up for a wrong

questions.feedback_correct: Gawain bore something hard, and now he is forgiven.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read the words after it: absolved and forgiven. Forgiven for what?

quizzes.title: Week 3 Language Check: Adjectives and adverbs
quizzes.description:
Week 3 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · Module 3 · Week 3
20 points10 questionsOpen notesOne try
Questions 1 to 5 · Grammar
Adjectives and adverbs
 
Questions 6 to 10 · Words
contemptuouslyscullionancestrybesiegedhomage
Done when
 
☐All 10 answered
☐Submitted (one try)
☐I read the feedback on any I missed

questions.text: Which word in this sentence is an adverb? "Beaumains answered the Lady Linnet politely."
questions.feedback_correct: Politely tells how he answered, so it describes the verb.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Which word tells how the action was done?

questions.text: "The Lady Linnet rode away on her white palfrey." The word white is
questions.feedback_correct: White describes the palfrey, a noun.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Ask what white describes: the horse, a thing.

questions.text: In which sentence is the -ly word an adjective?

answers.text: Beaumains came suddenly before the King.
Kay gave him every lowly task in the kitchen.

questions.feedback_correct: Lowly describes the task, a noun, so it is an adjective even though it ends in -ly.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Three of these describe how someone acted. Which one describes a thing?

questions.text: The stranger stands "a head ___ than either" of the two serving men.
questions.feedback_correct: Two things compared: the comparative, taller.
questions.feedback_incorrect: He is compared with each man, one at a time. Two things need -er, and never more + -er.

questions.text: Linnet mocks him, and Gareth answers ___. Which adverb is the most precise?
questions.feedback_correct: Courteously names exactly how: with a knight's good manners.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Nicely and okay are vague, and good is an adjective. Which word shows the manner exactly?

questions.text: "He's neither of those," said Sir Kay contemptuously. Contemptuously means

answers.text: in a way that shows he thinks the other person is worthless
in a way that shows he is afraid

questions.feedback_correct: Kay looks down on the stranger.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Read what Kay says next: "not fit to mix with us knights."

questions.text: Linnet calls Beaumains "a filthy scullion." A scullion is

answers.text: a squire who carries a knight's shield
a servant who does the roughest kitchen work
a minstrel who sings at feasts

questions.feedback_correct: Kay put him to the kitchen's lowest work.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Linnet says it to insult him for where he has been working all year.

questions.text: "I am no scullion, but a gentleman born, and of nobler ancestry than you are!" Ancestry means

answers.text: the family line a person comes from

questions.feedback_correct: His father is King Lot and his mother is the King's sister.
questions.feedback_incorrect: He says he is a gentleman born. What does birth give you?

questions.text: Linnet says her sister is "besieged" in Castle Dangerous. Besieged means

answers.text: hidden away by magic so no one can find her
surrounded by an enemy so that no one can get in or out
locked in by her own family

questions.feedback_correct: The Red Knight's tents surround the castle.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look at the camp around the red castle.

questions.text: The knights Gareth spares ride to Camelot to "do homage" to King Arthur. To do homage is to

answers.text: promise loyalty and service to a lord or king
pay a fine for breaking the law
hold a feast in the king's honour

questions.feedback_correct: They come to serve Arthur.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The Blue Knight brings a hundred followers to serve the King. What are they promising?

quizzes.title: Week 4 Language Check: Sentence types and conjunctions
quizzes.description:
Week 4 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · Module 3 · Week 4
20 points10 questionsOpen notesOne try
Questions 1 to 5 · Grammar
Sentence types and conjunctions
 
Questions 6 to 10 · Words
siegelineagedeclinedaccomplisheddesolate
Done when
 
☐All 10 answered
☐Submitted (one try)
☐I read the feedback on any I missed

questions.text: What kind of sentence is "Galahad drew the sword from the stone, and he slid it into the sheath at his side."?
questions.feedback_correct: Two complete thoughts joined by a comma and and.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Count the complete thoughts and look for the comma + joining word.

questions.text: What kind of sentence is "When the Holy Grail entered the hall, none could speak a word."?
questions.feedback_correct: "When the Holy Grail entered the hall" cannot stand alone.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Can the part starting with When stand alone?

questions.text: Which word is the subordinating conjunction in "Percivale joined the pieces after he had prayed to God."?
questions.feedback_correct: After begins the part that leans on the rest.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Find the word that starts a part that cannot stand alone.

questions.text: Which word shows contrast? "Arthur called Launcelot the best knight in the world, ___ Launcelot would not try to draw the sword."
questions.feedback_correct: But shows the two ideas pull against each other.
questions.feedback_incorrect: So, because and for show cause; which word shows a turn?

questions.text: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

answers.text: Because the Grail was so bright no one, could look at it.
Because the Grail was so bright, no one could look at it.
The Grail was so bright, no one could look at it.
Because, the Grail was so bright no one could look at it.

questions.feedback_correct: The leaning part comes first, so a comma follows it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Two sentences joined by only a comma make a comma splice. The comma belongs right after the part that starts with Because.

questions.text: "Every seat was full except for the Siege Perilous." In this story, a siege is

answers.text: an army camped around a castle

questions.feedback_correct: Siege is an old word for a seat.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Today siege can mean an army around a castle; at the Round Table it names a seat.

questions.text: Naciens brings "a young knight of royal lineage." Lineage means

answers.text: the family line a person comes from
a promise made to a king

questions.feedback_correct: Galahad comes from a royal family line.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Lineage is about family, not training, armour or promises.

questions.text: "Each of them declined the rich fare and the strong wine." Declined means
questions.feedback_correct: They said no and ate only bread.
questions.feedback_incorrect: What did they eat instead?

questions.text: Naciens tells the three knights, "this night all things shall be accomplished." Accomplished means
questions.feedback_correct: That night the quest is brought to its end: Galahad receives the Grail and Pelles is healed.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A feast is happening, but Naciens means something more. What happens to the quest that night?

questions.text: The lands around Carbonek "were never more waste or desolate." Desolate means
questions.feedback_correct: Before the quest ended, the land was waste and lifeless.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Never more means it used to be this way. What was the Waste Land like?

quizzes.title: Week 5 Language Check: Paragraphs and quoting evidence
quizzes.description:
Week 5 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · Module 3 · Week 5
20 points10 questionsOpen notesOne try
Questions 1 to 5 · Grammar
Paragraphs and quoting evidence
 
Questions 6 to 10 · Words
treasoncounseltrucebrandishedendured
Done when
 
☐All 10 answered
☐Submitted (one try)
☐I read the feedback on any I missed

questions.text: In a paragraph about Gawain, which sentence makes the best topic sentence?

answers.text: "Gawain dies after the landing at Dover."
"Gawain's anger finally gives way to forgiveness."
Green writes, "Then Gawain asked for pen and ink."
"Gawain has brothers named Gareth and Gaheris."

questions.feedback_correct: A topic sentence states one point the paragraph can prove.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Where Gawain dies and who his brothers are: facts with nothing to prove. The pen-and-ink line is evidence, not a point.

questions.text: Which sentence punctuates the quotation correctly?

answers.text: Bors said "I counsel you not to go this night".
Bors said, "I counsel you not to go this night".
Bors said, "I counsel you not to go this night."
Bors said: I counsel you not to go this night.

questions.feedback_correct: A comma after said, and the period inside the closing mark.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look for the comma before the quotation and the period inside the last quotation mark.

questions.text: A student writes: Arthur says of Lucan, "he had more need of help than I had." Which sentence is real elaboration?

answers.text: "This shows Arthur cares more about his knight's pain than his own."

questions.feedback_correct: Elaboration explains what the evidence proves.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The other three add facts; none explains the quotation.

questions.text: What are the three parts of a body paragraph, in order?
questions.feedback_correct: Point, proof, then your explanation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Introduction, body, conclusion is the shape of a whole essay. One paragraph goes point, proof, explanation.

questions.text: Which is the best evidence for the topic sentence "Launcelot stays loyal to Arthur even in war"?

answers.text: "Launcelot fights Gawain three times in France."
"When Bors could strike down the king, Launcelot stops him and helps Arthur onto his own horse."
"Launcelot rides home to Joyous Garde with his followers."

questions.feedback_correct: This moment shows loyalty to Arthur in the middle of a battle.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Which choice shows Launcelot protecting the king himself?

questions.text: Agravain wants Launcelot accused of treason. Treason is
questions.feedback_correct: Mordred's seizing of the crown is treason too.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A deadly wound is mortal; an agreement to stop fighting is a truce; a long, flat boat is a barge.

questions.text: Bors tells Launcelot, "I counsel you not to go this night." To counsel is to
questions.feedback_correct: Bors advises; Launcelot does not take the advice.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Bors is not giving an order. What is a friend doing when he says 'I would not, if I were you'?

questions.text: Gawain's spirit tells Arthur to make a truce with Mordred for one month. A truce is

answers.text: an agreement to stop fighting for a time

questions.feedback_correct: A truce pauses a war.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Gawain wants to buy time until Launcelot comes. What would do that?

questions.text: "Three times it brandished the sword on high." Brandished means
questions.feedback_correct: The arm waves Excalibur high, three times.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sword is held 'on high'. What does a hand do with a sword held high?

questions.text: "Always the belief endured in Britain... that he would come again." Endured means
questions.feedback_correct: The belief lasted for centuries.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The sentence begins 'never was King Arthur forgotten'. So did the belief fade, or last?

quizzes.title: Week 6 Language Check: Sentence variety and editing
quizzes.description:
Week 6 Language Check
6th Grade ELA · Module 3 · Week 6
20 points10 questionsOpen notesOne try
Questions 1 to 5 · Grammar
Sentence variety and editing
 
Questions 6 to 10 · Words
patienthumilityallegiancepridefaithful
Done when
 
☐All 10 answered
☐Submitted (one try)
☐I read the feedback on any I missed

questions.text: Which is the best way to combine "Gareth serves in the kitchen for a year. Gareth never answers Sir Kay back."

answers.text: Gareth serves in the kitchen for a year, Gareth never answers Sir Kay back.
Gareth serves in the kitchen for a year and never answers Sir Kay back.
Gareth serves in the kitchen for a year and Gareth never answers and Sir Kay talks back.
Gareth serves. In the kitchen. Never answers Sir Kay.

questions.feedback_correct: The best version shares the subject and joins the two ideas. Two sentences joined by only a comma make a comma splice; the and-chain changes the meaning; the choppy version breaks into fragments.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The best version shares the subject and joins the two ideas. Two sentences joined by only a comma make a comma splice; the and-chain changes the meaning; the choppy version breaks into fragments.

questions.text: Which version opens with something other than the subject? "Gawain comes into the wild lands of North Wales after many days."

answers.text: Gawain, after many days, comes, into the wild lands of North Wales.
Gawain comes after many days into the wild lands of North Wales.
After many days, Gawain comes into the wild lands of North Wales.
Gawain comes into North Wales and its wild lands after many days.

questions.feedback_correct: "After many days" opens with a time phrase. The other choices still start with "Gawain," and one adds commas that break the sentence.
questions.feedback_incorrect: "After many days" opens with a time phrase. The other choices still start with "Gawain," and one adds commas that break the sentence.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a correlative pair (neither ... nor) correctly?

answers.text: Gareth asks for neither horse nor armour, only meat and drink.
Gareth asks for neither horse or armour, only meat and drink.
Gareth asks for either horse nor armour, only meat and drink.
Gareth neither asks for horse, armour, only meat and drink.

questions.feedback_correct: Neither always pairs with nor; either pairs with or.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Neither always pairs with nor; either pairs with or.

questions.text: Which edit keeps the whole sentence in the literary present? "Gawain hides the green lace, but later he told the Green Knight he was ashamed."

answers.text: Gawain hid the green lace, but later he tells the Green Knight he is ashamed.
Gawain hides the green lace, but later he will tell the Green Knight he was ashamed.
Gawain hides the green lace, but later he told the Green Knight he is ashamed.
Gawain hides the green lace, but later he tells the Green Knight he is ashamed.

questions.feedback_correct: Every verb about the book stays present: hides, tells, is.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Every verb about the book stays present: hides, tells, is.

questions.text: Launcelot says, "I knew well that I was never the best." Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

answers.text: Launcelot says, "I knew well that I was never the best." (208)
Launcelot says, "I knew well that I was never the best" (208).
Launcelot says "I knew well that I was never the best (208)."
Launcelot says, I knew well that I was never the best (208).

questions.feedback_correct: Comma before the quotation, the page after the closing mark, the period last.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Comma before the quotation, the page after the closing mark, the period last.

questions.text: For a whole year in the kitchen, Gareth is "always gentle and patient, never answering Sir Kay back." Patient means

answers.text: calm and willing to put up with trouble without complaining

questions.feedback_correct: He bears Kay's mockery for a year without answering back.
questions.feedback_incorrect: He bears Kay's mockery for a year without answering back.

questions.text: Merlin tells Arthur that from now on he will hold his sword "in all humility, and draw it only to defend the right." Humility means

answers.text: a modest view of your own importance
a promise made to a king

questions.feedback_correct: Arthur has just put away "all the pride and wilfulness."
questions.feedback_incorrect: Arthur has just put away "all the pride and wilfulness."

questions.text: Gareth tells the knight he has spared to go to Camelot and "do allegiance to King Arthur." Allegiance is

answers.text: a prize won at a tournament
a castle given to a knight
the loyalty owed to a ruler

questions.feedback_correct: The spared knight must serve Arthur from now on.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The spared knight must serve Arthur from now on.

questions.text: Dying at Dover, Gawain says he has been "mad with wicked pride and anger." Pride, as Gawain means it, is

answers.text: thinking too highly of yourself, so that you will not give way

questions.feedback_correct: His pride kept him from making peace; now he forgives.
questions.feedback_incorrect: His pride kept him from making peace; now he forgives.

questions.text: After the queen is rescued, "All the knights who remained faithful" to King Arthur beg him to make war on Launcelot. Faithful means
questions.feedback_correct: These knights stay loyal to the king when the Round Table splits.
questions.feedback_incorrect: These knights stay loyal to the king when the Round Table splits.

discussions.title: All-Class Forum 1 — Did Gawain Pass the Test?
discussions.html:
Did Gawain Pass the Test?
All-Class Forum 1 · Weeks 2 and 3
25 points1 post + 2 repliesOpens Week 2Closes end of Week 3
Did Gawain pass the test?
He kept the appointment at the Green Chapel. He kept back the green lace, and knew it.
Three moves
 
1
Post
your answer
→
2
Read
posts unlock after yours
→
3
Reply
two classmates
Your post
 
›Sentence one: passed, failed, or passed with a flaw.
›Name one moment from the tale.
›Answer the strongest objection:
Say passed? Answer this: he swore to hand over all he won, hid the lace on purpose, and says, “I betrayed my oath of knighthood.”

Say failed? Answer this: he hid it to save his life, and the Green Knight calls that “a little sin.”

Passed with a flaw? Answer both.
Your replies
 
Add
A second piece of evidence.
Challenge
A weak spot, and why.
Ask
A question they can answer.
“I agree” is not a reply.
Ground rules
 
›Complete sentences. Disagree with the idea, not the person.
›Book questions go in the Questions about the book thread.
Done when
 
☐My first sentence takes a position.
☐I named a moment and answered the objection.
☐I replied twice: add, challenge, or ask.
